title: IRGNN: A Graph-based Framework Integrating Numerical Solution and Point Cloud for Static IR Drop Prediction
problem: IR drop analysis in on-chip power grids is computationally expensive; traditional numerical methods are accurate but slow, while CNN-based ML methods lose fine-grained topology and PG structure information.
motivation: As ICs scale to advanced nodes, IR drop verification dominates design closure time; ML acceleration is essential but must preserve power grid interpretability.
method: The method uses a two-part approach: it first runs a numerical solver called AMG-PCG (which finds approximate solutions without fully solving the system) to create initial rough estimates of where power is lost in the chip's power grid, then uses graph-based machine learning to refine them. It represents the power grid nodes as a point cloud—a set of interconnected points—and feeds this into a graph transformer, a type of neural network that learns how nodes relate to each other based on their connections. The key innovation is a technique called Neighbor Distance Attention (NDA) that weights nearby nodes based on physical distance, allowing the model to capture both local fine-grained details and large-scale patterns in how power distributes across the grid.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using graph-based learning to make precise per-node power-loss predictions, rather than CNN methods that only produce rough grid-level maps, while grounding these predictions in accurate numerical solutions.
contributions: Novel graph-based framework (IRGNN + IRGraph) for node-wise IR drop prediction
Neighbor Distance Attention layer for topology-aware feature aggregation
Integration of numerical solutions (AMG-PCG) as interpretability foundation
Achieves higher accuracy than CNN-based methods and standard solvers with reduced runtime

metrics.accuracy: higher than CNN-based and numerical solvers

primary_theme: Graph-based IR drop prediction with numerical grounding
